question.text: A bondholder is committed to buying Rs. 500 crore of a new 10-year GOI bond at next week's auction and fears that bond prices may fall before the position can be sold in the secondary market. What should the bondholder do?

answer.text: Sell (short) 10-year GOI bond futures to hedge the price-decline risk
Buy 10-year GOI bond futures to add to the long position
Buy MIBOR futures to earn interest on the bond purchase amount
Do nothing since the position must be absorbed at the auction

explanation.text: The Logic: Holders or underwriters of bonds who expect interest rates to rise (and bond prices to fall) hedge by selling GOI bond futures. The short futures position gains as prices fall, offsetting the loss on the cash bond position - this is a classic short-hedge / hedge against future borrowing or future bond holdings illustrated in the workbook. The Trap: Buying bond futures doubles the long exposure; MIBOR futures hedge short-term interest accruals, not bond price risk; doing nothing leaves the price-decline risk unhedged. Note: The short-hedge pattern - sell futures now to lock in price, unwind once the cash bond position is disposed of - is the standard textbook application of GOI bond futures for any holder of bonds facing price-decline risk.
